description: Auth, service catalog, and provider availability. The base everyone books on top of.

issues.title: Project scaffold: Next.js + TypeScript + Prisma + Vitest
issues.body:
## Context
Source: AGENT.md §1. Nothing can be built until the stack exists.

## Task
Scaffold the app: Next.js (App Router), TypeScript strict, Prisma with a Postgres datasource, Vitest, ESLint/Prettier, and a `.env.example`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pnpm dev` boots a landing page.
- [ ] `pnpm test` runs (one placeholder test green).
- [ ] Prisma schema file exists with the User model from SPEC.md §5.
- [ ] `.env.example` has DATABASE_URL and SESSION_SECRET placeholders (no real secrets).

issues.title: Auth: signup, login, session cookie, role support
issues.body:
## Context
Source: SPEC.md §7, AGENT.md §2. Every other feature needs a signed-in user with a role.

## Task
Implement `POST /api/auth/signup` and `POST /api/auth/login`. Hash passwords, set an httpOnly session cookie, support roles CUSTOMER/PROVIDER/ADMIN.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Passwords hashed (never stored plaintext).
- [ ] Session cookie is httpOnly + Secure + SameSite; regenerated on login.
- [ ] Signup rejects duplicate email and invalid input (Zod).
- [ ] Unit tests for the auth service pass; no PII in logs.

issues.title: Service catalog: create + browse + filter by category
issues.body:
## Context
Source: SPEC.md §6-§7. Customers browse services; providers create them.

## Task
Implement `GET /api/services` (with `?category`), `GET /api/services/:id`, and `POST /api/services` (provider only). Build `/services` and `/services/:id` pages.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `POST /api/services` is provider-only (403 otherwise), input validated.
- [ ] `GET /api/services?category=` filters correctly.
- [ ] `/services` lists active services; `/services/:id` shows detail.
- [ ] Tests cover the provider-only authorization check.

issues.title: Provider availability: set weekly windows
issues.body:
## Context
Source: SPEC.md §5 Availability, §7 PUT /api/availability.

## Task
Implement `PUT /api/availability` (provider only) storing weekday + startMin/endMin windows, and a `/provider/availability` page to edit them.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Provider can set multiple windows per weekday.
- [ ] Validation rejects startMin >= endMin and out-of-range minutes.
- [ ] Only the owning provider can edit their availability (server-side check).
- [ ] Unit tests for validation + ownership pass.
